result.title: Imitating the Imperfect: Offline-to-Online Robust Imitation Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrators
result.summary: Imitation learning (IL) typically relies on large-scale offline demonstrations collected from multiple human or algorithmic demonstrators. However, most existing approaches assume these demonstrators are homogeneous or near-optimal experts, a convenient but unrealistic assumption in real-world applications. In practice, demonstrations are often collected from heterogeneous demonstrators with unknown and varying levels of expertise, resulting in highly mixed-quality data. In this work, we study a challenging yet practical setting of imitation learning from such heterogeneous imperfect demonstrators. We propose Latent Expertise and Optimality Scoring based Imitation Learning (LEOS-IL), a principled framework that jointly learns (i) a state-action optimality scoring model and (ii) latent expertise levels for each demonstrator from unlabeled suboptimal offline demonstrations. The learned scoring model is then integrated into an online policy optimization procedure, where the agent is trained to maximize estimated optimality scores while its online rollouts are iteratively leveraged to refine the scoring model, thereby mitigating distributional shift during online adaptation. We further provide theoretical guarantees for optimality score identification and conditional optimal occupancy and policy recovery under explicit sufficient conditions. Experiments on continuous control benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing baselines across highly heterogeneous and low-quality demonstration regimes.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究由异构、次优且未知水平示范者提供的模仿学习，提出 LEOS-IL：从无标注示范中联合学习状态-动作最优性评分模型与每个示范者的 latent expertise，再把评分模型接入在线策略优化并迭代精化，同时给出可识别性与策略恢复的理论条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用 latent 变量刻画数据来源的隐含质量、再由评分模型反推可靠监督的思路，可能为 LVR 中混合质量推理轨迹的贡献分配与监督加权提供概念类比，但领域为连续控制 IL，需核查迁移可行性。
